Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete slab block on massive pilotis, with deep eggcrate loggias, rear access galleries, a freestanding lift and stair tower at one end and a roof terrace with plant and a vaulted pavilion.
spec.layout: Static architectural model, 1 unit = 1 m, built at full real size. +Z is the long front facade, +Y is up, and the model is centred on x = 0. The long slab runs along X from x=-32 (right end seen from the front, the model's right) to x=18. It sits on pilotis: a 6 m open ground storey, then 7 residential storeys of 3 m each (y=6 to 27), then a roof terrace from 27 to about 31. The tower is a separate heavy concrete shaft with a cantilevered crown at the left end (x 18 to 32) and is the tallest element at y=31. Grid: 10 structural bays of 5 m on the slab at x edges -32,-27,...,18 (edge i = -32+5i). Storey floor levels are y=6+3k, k=0..7. The slab core is a solid block x[-32,18], y[6,27], z[-7.5,7.5]. FRONT (+Z) is an eggcrate of deep loggias: concrete party fins at every bay line and floor and ceiling slabs project from the core wall at z=7.5 out to z=11. Each loggia is 4.65 m wide and 2.65 m high and 3.5 m deep. The loggia back walls are painted panels in rotating primaries, with glazed sliding doors, railings and planters. BACK (-Z) is the access side: continuous gallery decks at each storey projecting from z=-7.5 to z=-9.5 with solid 1.1 m parapets, and three full-height stair towers projecting to z=-11. The GROUND storey has massive tapered piloti columns, transfer beams, a recessed glazed lobby, an entrance canopy, steps and a ramp. The ROOF has a parapet, plant rooms, chimney-like ventilation stacks, a water tank and a vaulted concrete pavilion. STYLE: raw concrete brutalism. Heavy, blocky, chunky proportions. Every concrete surface is built from several flat greys, so that the pour lines and wear read as geometry. Board-marking is thin horizontal strips about 3 cm proud in boardMark. Tie-rod holes are small dark discs on a regular grid. Cast joints are thin dark recessed strips. Rain staining is vertical streaks in stain and mossStain, below ledges, parapets and window heads. Rust runs sit under metal fixings. Concrete tones vary between neighbouring panels (concreteLight, concreteMid, concreteWarm, concreteDark) so the pour sequence shows. Colour comes only in small doses: the loggia panels, lit windows, doors and plants. No smooth or glossy surfaces. Chamfers are minimal, edges are crisp, and geometry is boxes, slabs, wedges and half-cylinders. Do not add scenery, ground, trees or props beyond the subject and the listed planters, bike racks and lamps.

parts.builds: The solid mass of the residential slab, x[-32,18], y[6,27], z[-7.5,7.5], and its two end gables. Use several adjacent concrete boxes in different grey tones (concreteLight, concreteMid, concreteWarm), one per pour lift, with a thin shadowRecess cast joint between lifts every 3 m of height and board-marking strips on every face. Build the front wall (z=7.5) and back wall (z=-7.5) as plain concrete planes, with sliding-door and gallery-door openings left to the facade parts. Build a thin roof slab edge band at y=26.7-27. Add vertical expansion joints (shadowRecess strips) at x=-7 and x=3. Add tie-rod hole grids on the walls at both ends. Left gable x=-32 and right gable x=18, the latter partly hidden behind the tower: a large blank concrete wall with a tall narrow stair-light slit, a big white painted storey-number emblem built from small boxes, rain streaks (stain, mossStain) and a rust stain under the roof edge. Deep concreteDark soffit strip along the underside at y=6. Do not build loggias, galleries, fins, windows or panels. Those belong to the front and back facade parts.
parts.attaches: Sits on the pilotis and transfer beams at pilotisTop (y=6). Its front wall at frontCoreWall (z=7.5) and back wall at backCoreWall (z=-7.5) are where the facade parts attach. Its roof top at slabRoofTop (y=27) is where the roof part stands. The right gable abuts the tower at towerJoin (x=18).

parts.builds: The +Z loggia eggcrate, z[7.5,11], 10 bays by 7 storeys. Build concrete party fins, 0.35 m thick, at each of the 11 bay lines x=-32+5i, running full height y[6,27] and z[7.5,11], with board-marking strips and alternate tone variation. Build floor and ceiling slabs 0.35 m thick at each storey level y=6+3k (k=0..7), spanning the full width and projecting from z=7.5 to z=11, with a darker front-edge band and rain streaks down from slab edges. Inside each loggia, 4.65 m by 2.65 m, add a coloured painted back-wall panel just proud of z=7.5 (panelRed, panelOchre, panelBlue, panelWhite and panelGreen in a pseudo-random but deterministic pattern, about one in three loggias left raw concrete). Add a glazed sliding door in frameDark and glass with a glassLit interior on about one in four, and a solid timber door leaf. Add a metalRail balustrade at the slab front edge in about half the loggias, and a planter box with planterSoil and plantGreen in some. Add an occasional hanging laundry line or a chair block. Every bay at the top storey gets a deeper concreteDark shadow strip under the roof slab. A horizontal pair of thin signWhite house-number plates at the left end. Use boxes, not tubes, for rails (thin posts and a top bar).
parts.attaches: Backs onto the core wall at frontCoreWall (z=7.5). The outer frame edge lies at frontLoggiaEdge (z=11). Its bottom slab sits at y=6 on the pilotis, and its top slab reaches y=27, where the roof parapet starts.

parts.builds: The -Z access side, z[-11,-7.5]. Build continuous gallery decks 0.4 m thick at each storey y=6+3k (k=0..7) projecting from z=-7.5 to z=-9.5, over x[-32,18]. Add 1.1 m solid concrete parapets on the outer edge with a metalRail top bar, board-marked and rain-stained. On the core wall behind, one entrance per 5 m bay: a timber door in frameDark with a small glassLit window beside it, a doormat or number plate in signWhite, and a thin concrete canopy slab over every other door. Between doors, a long high kitchen window in frameDark and glass. Build 3 full-height stair towers at x centres -22, -4 and 12, each 4.5 m wide, running y[6,27] and projecting to z=-11. They are heavy concrete (concreteDark and concreteMid) with tall narrow vertical slit windows (glass with a glassLit stripe) and a flat cantilevered cap slab at y=27, with board-marking and stains. Add connecting bridge decks at each tower where the gallery meets it, and a cluster of drainpipes (thin metalRail boxes) at the bay lines. Vertical rust streaks below the parapet fixings.
parts.attaches: Backs onto the core wall at backCoreWall (z=-7.5). Gallery edge at backGalleryEdge (z=-9.5), stair-tower faces at backStairTowerEdge (z=-11). Bottom at y=6 on the pilotis, top at y=27 under the roof parapet.

parts.builds: The open pilotis storey, y[0,6], x[-32,18], z[-11,11], resting on the floor. Build massive tapered piloti columns, each a pair of stacked frustums or chunky tapered boxes about 1.6 m by 3.2 m at the base and 2.4 m by 3.6 m at the top, with board-marking and rough concreteDark lower sections where splashed. Place them in two rows at z=-5.5 and z=5.5, at x=-27, -17, -7, 3 and 13, plus a heavier pair at each end. Add transfer beams at y[5,6] along each row and across between the rows (concreteMid), which fill the underside under the slab. A recessed glazed lobby box at x[-10,0], z[-5,5], y[0,4.6] with frameDark mullions, glass, a glassLit interior, a sign above the door and a timber double door. An entrance canopy slab projecting forward to z=11 at x[-10,0] and y=4.6-5, and wide concrete steps and a ramp with metalRail handrails at lobbyDoor. A low plinth strip along the front. Cycle store: a row of bike racks with simple wheel frames. Planter boxes with planterSoil and plantGreen. Two tall post lamps with glassLit heads. A big painted 'blok' lettering, or signWhite house number emblem, on a pier. Concrete splash stains and moss near the bottom of piers, and rain streaks.
parts.attaches: Top face at y=6 (pilotisTop) carries the slab core, front facade and back galleries. The tower stands at towerJoin (x=18) immediately to its right. The lobby door is at lobbyDoor (x=-5, z=11).

parts.builds: The freestanding concrete lift and stair tower at the left end, x[18,32], z[-7.5,7.5], y[0,31], resting on the floor and abutting the slab end gable at towerJoin (x=18). The shaft is a stacked set of boxes (different concrete tones and pour lifts, each 3 m) with board-marking, tie-rod grids, expansion joint strips and heavy rain and moss staining. The base is wider and darker (concreteDark) up to y=2. Vertical full-height glazed slits, glass with frameDark mullions and a stripe of glassLit, on the +Z face and on the +X end, with deep concreteDeep reveals. A projecting stair-landing bay on the front face: small cantilevered balconies, 1.5 m deep, at y=6,12,18 and 24, with solid parapets. Link bridges to the slab at y=6+3k, as short concrete decks between x=17 and x=19. The CROWN, y[27,31]: a heavy cantilevered concrete box on top overhanging the shaft by 0.8 m on the front and sides (a wide band of shadowRecess underneath), with a strip window ribbon and a flat roof slab, and a small signWhite emblem plus a red panelRed stripe on the +X face. A rooftop crane or lift motor box, 2 chimney stacks, a lightning rod (thin metalRail box, 1.5 m, no taller than y=31) and aviation lights as small glowing panelRed boxes. Rust streaks under the crown overhang.
parts.attaches: Its -X face meets the slab right gable at towerJoin (x=18). Its link decks align with the slab storey levels y=6+3k. Its crown base at towerCrownBase is y=27, flush with the slab roof level.

parts.builds: Everything on the slab roof, y[27,31], x[-32,18], z[-9,9]. A continuous concrete parapet 1.2 m high (y 27 to 28.2) around the slab, set at z=±7.5 and x=-32 and 18, with a thin coping slab in concreteLight, board-marking, rain stains and scuppers (shadowRecess boxes) every 5 m with long vertical stains below. A flat roof deck in concreteMid with expansion joint lines. A vaulted concrete pavilion (a half-cylinder or arch-shaped barrel roof about 12 m long, 5 m wide, 3.5 m high) at x[-20,-8], with glazed end walls (glass and frameDark, glassLit inside) and chunky piers. A rectangular plant room with louvres at x[0,10], z[-4,4], 2.6 m high, and a water tank (a drum of metalRail with stair ladder and rust bands). 5 ventilation stacks of various heights, up to y=31, in concreteDark with cap slabs. A row of skylights, small pyramids or boxes in glass. A running track or sundeck ellipse is not needed. Add low wall benches, a few planters with plantGreen shrubs along the parapet, and a flagpole no taller than y=31. Rust and moss patches on the roof deck.
parts.attaches: Stands on the slab roof at slabRoofTop (y=27). Its parapet follows the outer edge of the front facade top slab (z=11 is not covered, so the parapet stays at z≤7.5, or overhangs to z=11 only as a thin coping slab) and the back gallery top. Roof deck reference at roofDeck.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the spec for a static brutalist housing block, no joints, thinking through realistic dimensions like a multi-storey slab around 20-24m tall and 56-60m long, with a pilotis base.

Now I'm working out the orientation so the long facade faces +Z, landing on a size roughly [64, 31, 22], with a body raised on chunky piloti up to about 6m, seven storeys of slab above, and a roof terrace with plant equipment. I'm also placing a taller stair/lift tower at one end of the block to break up the massing.

Breaking the design into five parts, starting with the pilotis and ground level: tapered board-marked concrete columns, entrance lobbies, canopy, ramp, and steps forming a plinth beneath the main slab.

Next I'm planning the slab itself, splitting it into a solid structural core (concrete mass, end gables, floor plates, and rear facade) separate from the front facade's loggia grid, balconies, brise-soleil, and windows, sharing mounting points between the front and back facade planes for alignment.

Splitting the gable ends between front and back halves feels awkward, so I'm reconsidering the division: instead, let the slab core part own the entire volume including floor plates, end walls, and party-wall fins, while the front facade part owns everything attached beyond z>9.5 like balconies, brise-soleil, and window assemblies.

That gives six parts total (slab core, front, back, ground, tower, roof), with a combined budget of 900 split across them. I'm planning the concrete detailing for richness—board-marked bands, slab edges, expansion joints, stair slit windows, murals, tie-rod holes, stains—and sketching the concrete color palette with light and mid tones.

Rounding out the palette now with warm concrete, board-mark, stain, moss, rust, shadow recess, glass (plain and lit with a warm glow), dark frames, and accent panel colors (red, ochre, blue-grey, white), plus metal railing, timber, soil/plant greens, and signage white—capping it at 24 total colors for the loggia and accent details.

Now I'm working out the building's mounting coordinates—front and back slab faces, the pilotis top level, roof slab, gable end extent, and tower join point—along with storey heights of 3 meters stacked from a base of 6, and laying out the front facade into bay divisions roughly 5 meters wide spanning the 50-meter width.

I'm separating the core structure from the loggia system: the core's front wall sits recessed, while the loggia floor slabs and party-wall fins project forward to form balconies, with brise-soleil frames extending even further out as sun-shading elements.

For the back facade, I'm placing stair towers with slit windows and continuous access galleries at every storey, each with solid parapets, projecting back from the main wall plane to give depth and rhythm to the rear elevation.

For the side tower, I'm working out a blank concrete shaft with lift slits and cantilevered vertical windows, topped with an overhanging boxy crown, then reconciling its width against the slab core so the join at x=18 lines up cleanly, with the tower rising to the full building height of 31 while the roof pavilion and chimneys cap out just below that.

For the ground floor, I'm planning the piloti grid beneath the slab, with tapered columns spaced roughly every 10 meters in two rows flanking the center, plus a recessed glass lobby box, entrance canopy, ramp, steps, and small site furnishings like bike storage and planters, all sitting on a low podium slab that meets the core's underside at y=6.

I'm deciding the core owns the slab itself while the ground floor owns the transfer beams running up to that same datum, and I'm planning simple flat-colored materials throughout with no joints or bones needed since everything builds as static boxes. For details, I'll add board-marked concrete texture as thin proud strips and small dark discs for tie-rod holes, keeping everything at real-world meter scale with low geometry segment counts.

Now I'm working out the actual bounding boxes for each structural volume — the slab core, front and back facades, ground floor, and tower — figuring out how the tower's crown cantilever and end gable should align with the core's end wall so nothing clips or leaves gaps where they meet at x=18.

For the roof I'm setting its box to span from the core's top down to where the tower begins, keeping chimneys rising above the parapet, then dividing a budget of 900 total across the six elements (core, front, back, ground, tower, roof) so each gets a proportional share. I'm also sketching the layout grid — ten 5m bays along x and seven 3m storeys along y — to place loggia units per bay per floor.

I'm defining each storey's loggia as 5m wide and 3m tall, framed by thick concrete party-wall fins at every bay line and floor/ceiling slabs at each storey height, creating an eggcrate pattern of open loggias roughly 4.65 by 2.65 meters with 3.5m depth, with painted back walls set slightly forward as part of the front facade.

Now I'm adding glazing sliding doors on the core wall, plain concrete behind, and varying the loggias with coloured panels in a rotating palette, balcony railings, planters, lit windows, and laundry details for variety. For the back facade I'm setting up galleries at each storey level with parapets, doors, windows, and doormats per bay, plus placing stair towers at several x-positions along the building.
